description: Learn about the three types of rocks, rock formation processes, how to identify minerals, and the many uses of rocks and minerals in daily life

slides.title: Welcome to Rocks & Minerals
slides.content:
# Rocks and Minerals - Earth's Building Blocks

The solid Earth beneath your feet is made of **rocks and minerals**. They form mountains, valleys, and even the soil we walk on.

## What You Will Learn:
- The three **types of rocks** and how they form
- How the **rock cycle** works
- How to **identify minerals**
- The many **uses** of rocks and minerals

## Rocks vs Minerals:
- A **mineral** is a naturally occurring solid with a specific chemical composition
- A **rock** is made up of one or more **minerals** combined together
- Example: **Granite** (rock) is made of quartz, feldspar, and mica (minerals)

## Fun Facts:
- The oldest rocks on Earth are about **4 billion years** old
- **Diamonds** are the hardest natural mineral
- The Earth's crust contains about **4,000 different minerals**
- Rocks are constantly being created, destroyed, and recycled

> **Under Your Feet:** Right now, you are standing on rocks that may be millions or even billions of years old!

slides.title: Igneous Rocks
slides.content:
# Igneous Rocks - Born from Fire

**Igneous rocks** form when hot, molten rock (magma or lava) cools and solidifies.

## How They Form:
- Deep inside the Earth, temperatures are so high that rock **melts** into **magma**
- When magma reaches the surface through volcanoes, it is called **lava**
- As magma or lava **cools**, it hardens into igneous rock

## Two Types:

### Intrusive Igneous Rocks:
- Form **inside** the Earth when magma cools slowly underground
- Cool **slowly** = large crystal grains (you can see them)
- Example: **Granite** - used for countertops, building stone

### Extrusive Igneous Rocks:
- Form **on the surface** when lava cools quickly
- Cool **quickly** = small or no visible crystals
- Example: **Basalt** - the most common rock on Earth's surface
- Example: **Obsidian** - volcanic glass, very smooth and shiny
- Example: **Pumice** - so full of air holes it floats on water!

## Properties of Igneous Rocks:
- Usually very **hard and dense**
- Do NOT contain **fossils** (too hot when forming)
- Can have **crystals** visible (intrusive) or not (extrusive)
- Often found near **volcanoes** and areas of volcanic activity

| Feature | Intrusive | Extrusive |
|---------|-----------|----------|
| Where formed | Underground | On surface |
| Cooling speed | Slow | Fast |
| Crystal size | Large | Small/None |
| Examples | Granite, Gabbro | Basalt, Obsidian, Pumice |

> **Fire to Stone:** The word 'igneous' comes from the Latin word 'ignis' meaning fire. These are truly rocks born from fire!

slides.title: Sedimentary Rocks
slides.content:
# Sedimentary Rocks - Layered History

**Sedimentary rocks** form when small pieces of rock, sand, mud, or remains of living things are deposited in layers and compressed over time.

## How They Form:
1. **Weathering and erosion** break existing rocks into small pieces
2. Wind, water, or ice **transport** these pieces (sediments)
3. Sediments **settle** in layers at the bottom of rivers, lakes, and oceans
4. Over millions of years, layers are **compressed and cemented** together
5. They harden into sedimentary rock

## Types of Sedimentary Rocks:

### Clastic (From Rock Fragments):
- **Sandstone** - made of sand grains cemented together
- **Shale** - made of very fine clay and mud particles
- **Conglomerate** - made of rounded pebbles cemented in matrix

### Chemical (From Dissolved Minerals):
- **Limestone** - formed from calcium carbonate (often from shells)
- **Rock salt** - formed when salty water evaporates
- **Gypsum** - used in making plaster

### Organic (From Living Things):
- **Coal** - formed from compressed ancient plants
- **Chalk** - formed from microscopic shells
- **Fossil limestone** - contains visible fossils

## Special Feature - FOSSILS:
- Sedimentary rocks are the ONLY rocks that contain **fossils**
- Fossils are preserved remains of ancient **plants and animals**
- They help scientists understand Earth's **history**
- Fossil fuels (coal, oil, gas) form in sedimentary rocks

## Properties:
- Usually have visible **layers** (strata)
- Often **softer** than igneous rocks
- May contain **fossils**
- Cover about **75%** of Earth's land surface

> **Earth's Diary:** Sedimentary rocks are like pages in Earth's diary. Each layer tells the story of what happened at a different time in history!

slides.quizQuestion: Which type of rock is the ONLY type that can contain fossils?

slides.title: Metamorphic Rocks
slides.content:
# Metamorphic Rocks - Transformed by Heat and Pressure

**Metamorphic rocks** form when existing rocks are changed by extreme heat, pressure, or both, WITHOUT melting.

## How They Form:
- Existing rocks (igneous, sedimentary, or even other metamorphic) are subjected to:
  - Extreme **heat** (from nearby magma)
  - Extreme **pressure** (from being buried deep underground)
  - **Chemical processes** (hot fluids moving through rock)
- The minerals rearrange themselves into new patterns
- The rock **transforms** into a new type without melting

## The word 'Metamorphic':
- Comes from Greek: **meta** (change) + **morphe** (form)
- Literally means "changed form"

## Examples of Metamorphic Rocks:

| Original Rock | Becomes | Change |
|--------------|---------|--------|
| Limestone | **Marble** | Heat and pressure |
| Sandstone | **Quartzite** | Heat and pressure |
| Shale | **Slate** | Pressure |
| Granite | **Gneiss** | Extreme heat and pressure |
| Coal | **Diamond** | Extreme pressure deep underground |

## Properties:
- Often harder than the original rock
- May have **bands or layers** of different minerals
- Crystals may be **aligned** in the same direction
- Very **dense** and durable

## Famous Metamorphic Rocks:
- **Marble** - used for sculptures (Taj Mahal!), flooring, and countertops
- **Slate** - used for roofing tiles, blackboards, and flooring
- **Quartzite** - very hard, used for building and decoration
- **Diamond** - the hardest natural substance, used in jewelry and cutting tools

> **Pressure Makes Diamonds:** Just as coal transforms into diamonds under extreme pressure, challenges in life can transform you into something stronger and more beautiful!

slides.title: The Rock Cycle
slides.content:
# The Rock Cycle - Rocks Keep Changing!

Rocks are not permanent - they are constantly being **recycled** through the rock cycle.

## The Rock Cycle:

Any rock type can become any other rock type!

```
Igneous Rock
  |-- Weathering and Erosion --> Sediments --> Sedimentary Rock
  |-- Heat and Pressure --> Metamorphic Rock
  |-- Melting --> Magma --> (cools) --> Igneous Rock again

Sedimentary Rock
  |-- Heat and Pressure --> Metamorphic Rock
  |-- Weathering --> Sediments --> New Sedimentary Rock
  |-- Melting --> Magma --> Igneous Rock

Metamorphic Rock
  |-- Melting --> Magma --> Igneous Rock
  |-- Weathering --> Sediments --> Sedimentary Rock
  |-- More heat/pressure --> Different Metamorphic Rock
```

## Key Processes:
| Process | What Happens | Result |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| Cooling | Magma/lava solidifies | Igneous rock |
| Weathering | Rock breaks into pieces | Sediments |
| Compaction | Sediments pressed together | Sedimentary rock |
| Heat/Pressure | Rock structure changes | Metamorphic rock |
| Melting | Rock becomes liquid | Magma |

## The Cycle Is:
- **Continuous** - always happening somewhere
- **Very slow** - takes millions of years
- **Driven by** Earth's internal heat and the sun's energy
- **Never-ending** - has been running for billions of years

> **Constant Change:** The rocks under your school may once have been part of a volcanic mountain, then eroded into sand, then compressed into sandstone, and might one day melt back into magma!

slides.title: Minerals and Identification
slides.content:
# Minerals - The Building Blocks of Rocks

A **mineral** is a naturally occurring, solid substance with a definite chemical composition and crystal structure.

## Properties Used to Identify Minerals:

### 1. Color
- The most **obvious** property but NOT always reliable
- Some minerals come in many colors (quartz: clear, pink, purple)
- Some minerals always have the same color (sulfur: always yellow)

### 2. Hardness (Mohs Scale)
| Hardness | Mineral | Common Test |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| 1 | Talc | Scratched by fingernail |
| 2 | Gypsum | Scratched by fingernail |
| 3 | Calcite | Scratched by coin |
| 4 | Fluorite | Scratched by knife |
| 5 | Apatite | Scratched by knife (just) |
| 6 | Feldspar | Scratches glass |
| 7 | Quartz | Scratches glass easily |
| 8 | Topaz | Scratches quartz |
| 9 | Corundum | Very hard |
| 10 | Diamond | Hardest natural substance |

### 3. Luster (Shine)
- **Metallic** - shiny like metal (gold, pyrite)
- **Non-metallic** - glassy, waxy, dull, or pearly

### 4. Streak
- The color of the **powder** when mineral is rubbed on unglazed tile
- More reliable than color!
- Hematite: Looks gray but has a RED streak

### 5. Crystal Shape
- Minerals form specific geometric shapes
- Salt (halite): Cube-shaped crystals
- Quartz: Six-sided pointed crystals

> **Fool's Gold:** Pyrite looks like gold and has fooled many people! But real gold is soft (scratched by a coin), while pyrite is hard. That is why testing properties matters!

slides.title: Uses of Rocks and Minerals
slides.content:
# Uses of Rocks and Minerals

Rocks and minerals are essential in our daily lives!

## In Construction:
- **Granite** - building stone, countertops, monuments
- **Marble** - flooring, sculptures, decorative stone
- **Limestone** - making cement and concrete
- **Sandstone** - building material
- **Slate** - roofing tiles
- **Sand and gravel** - concrete, roads

## In Industry:
- **Iron ore** (hematite, magnetite) - making steel
- **Bauxite** - making aluminum
- **Copper ore** - electrical wiring
- **Silicon** (from quartz) - computer chips, glass
- **Petroleum** (from sedimentary rocks) - fuel, plastics
- **Coal** - electricity generation

## In Daily Life:
| Mineral/Rock | Everyday Use |
|-------------|-------------|
| Halite (salt) | Cooking, food preservation |
| Graphite | Pencil lead |
| Talc | Talcum powder |
| Quartz | Watches, electronics |
| Gypsum | Plaster, chalk |
| Clay | Pottery, bricks |
| Mica | Electrical insulation |

## In Jewelry:
- **Diamond** - the most valued gemstone
- **Ruby** - red corundum
- **Sapphire** - blue corundum
- **Emerald** - green beryl
- **Gold** - precious metal
- **Silver** - precious metal

## In Medicine:
- **Calcium carbonate** (limestone) - antacids
- **Zinc oxide** - skin creams
- **Iron** supplements from iron minerals
- **Kaolin** (clay) - digestive medicine

> **Rocks in Your Life:** Right now, you are using rocks and minerals - the glass in your window (silica), the metal in your pen (iron ore), the salt in your food, and even the graphite in your pencil!

slides.title: Summary and Key Points
slides.content:
# Summary: Rocks and Minerals

## Three Types of Rocks:
| Type | How Formed | Examples | Key Feature |
|------|-----------|----------|-------------|
| Igneous | Cooling of magma/lava | Granite, Basalt | Hard, no fossils |
| Sedimentary | Layers compressed | Sandstone, Limestone | Layered, has fossils |
| Metamorphic | Heat and pressure | Marble, Slate | Transformed, very hard |

## The Rock Cycle:
- Rocks constantly change from one type to another
- Driven by heat, pressure, weathering, and erosion
- Takes millions of years

## Minerals:
- Building blocks of rocks
- Identified by: color, hardness, luster, streak, crystal shape
- Mohs Scale: 1 (softest - Talc) to 10 (hardest - Diamond)

## Uses:
- **Construction:** Granite, marble, limestone, sandstone
- **Industry:** Iron ore, bauxite, copper, silicon
- **Daily life:** Salt, graphite, talc, quartz
- **Jewelry:** Diamond, ruby, sapphire, gold

## Key Facts:
- Rocks are **always changing** through the rock cycle
- Sedimentary rocks are the **only type with fossils**
- Minerals are identified by **physical properties**, not just color
- Rocks and minerals are **essential** for modern life

> **Congratulations!** You now understand the fascinating world of rocks and minerals. Next time you pick up a rock, think about its incredible journey through millions of years!
